learning_outcomes.text: The general objective of the course is to prepare the mechanical engineer to know the current trends in the field of structural design.

Develop competencies regarding the realization of an in-depth and multilateral analysis of both constructive solutions and the behavior of resistance structures, so that the mechanical engineer can make optimal design decisions.
Ensure specific competencies regarding the design of rational models of mechanical structures that respect the criteria of minimum weight, durability, and maximum operational safety.

syllabus_topics: Evaluation of Wind Action on Structures
Evaluation of Snow Action on Structures
Analytical Calculation of Structures and their Global Analysis using the Finite Element Method
Analytical Calculation and Finite Element Analysis of Different Types of Joints Used in the Realization of Metallic Structures
Case Study 1: Structural Failures Due to General Actions: Specific Weights, Self-Weights, Useful Loads for Buildings
Case Study 2: Structural Failures Due to Wind Action
Project: Calculation of Structures for the Distribution of Pressures, Forces, Stresses, and Deformations
teaching_methods: Methods for Developing Analytical, Innovative, and Critical Thinking
Study of Curricular Documents and Bibliography
assessment_rules: Awarding of credits for the discipline is conditional on obtaining a minimum final grade of 5. The final grade consists of the exam grade (1/2), the laboratory grade (1/4), and the project grade (1/4). Minimum knowledge required to pass includes knowing the basics of construction design and performing analytical and numerical calculation of a structure.
